question.problem:
In a particular shop, cables are sold in coils. The length of the cable in a coil is normally distributed with a mean of $50\,\text{m}$ and a standard deviation of $0.7\,\text{m}.$ If John bought $5$ coils, what is the probability that the total length of the cables he bought is greater than $250\,\text{m}$ and less than $253\,m?$ You may assume that the lengths of the cable in the coils are mutually independent.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution.*

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ | $\,0.03\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,1.7\,$ | $\,0.9554\,$ | $\,0.9564\,$ | $\,0.9573\,$ | $\,0.9582\,$ |
| $\,1.8\,$ | $\,0.9641\,$ | $\,0.9649\,$ | $\,0.9656\,$ | $\,0.9664\,$ |
| $\,1.9\,$ | $\,0.9713\,$ | $\,0.9719\,$ | $\,0.9726\,$ | $\,0.9732\,$ |
